solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Ally in SE Asian war zone used this

definitions.text: Ally in SE Asian war zone used this

indicators.note: in tells us the word for a friend sits inside the name of the war zone

parts.note: Nam is the informal name for Vietnam, the war zone of the 1960s and 70s
an ally is a friend, a pal

explanation.surface: A remark about the incendiary weapon dropped by allied forces in the Vietnam War.
explanation.walkthrough: An &lit: the container reading and the whole-clue description of the war weapon coincide, so every word does double service.
explanation.definitionFit: This jellied incendiary was notoriously dropped by American forces over Vietnam.

clue.text: Inquiring word after boy turned up —- but he didn't!

definitions.text: Inquiring word after boy turned up —- but he didn't!

indicators.note: after places the question word behind the reversed boy
in a down entry, turned up means the word for a boy is written bottom to top

parts.note: a boy is a son
how is a word used to ask a question

explanation.surface: A lad was supposed to show up, but never arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'turned up' reads the boy from bottom to top; the exclamation 'but he didn't!' makes the whole clue describe the absentee.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who books or is expected but fails to appear is called this, the absentee himself.

clue.text: Quiet little room cold, not very calming

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the abbreviation for cold is to stand where the abbreviation for very stood

parts.note: the 'smallest room' is a jocular name for the lavatory

explanation.surface: A remark that a small, quiet, chilly room is not especially soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold, not very' is a swap of one abbreviation for another; 'little room' is the British joke name 'the smallest room' for the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Placatory words are intended to appease, so they are soothing in effect.

clue.text: Tipple fit for a king? On the contrary!

indicators.note: on the contrary asks us to turn the phrase the other way round, here reading it backwards

parts.note: regal means royal, fit for a king

explanation.surface: Asking whether a drink is good enough for royalty, then saying the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' looks like a reply to the question, but it reverses REGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale beer is a common alcoholic drink, a tipple in British usage.

clue.text: Fish eating seaweed, producing hypothetical chemical

indicators.note: eating means the fish take the seaweed inside them

parts.note: ides are freshwater fish of the carp family
alga is a simple plant, a seaweed being one example

explanation.surface: Fish feeding on seaweed give rise to a theoretical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics a theoretical gas whose molecules do not interact is the standard idealised model.

clue.text: One beset by goddamned wind spoiled celebration for pensioners

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the letter for one is ringed by the other letters
spoiled signals that the swear word and the wind are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone troubled by a terrible wind ruins an anniversary party for an elderly couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges the two words and 'beset by' surrounds the numeral; a diamond anniversary marks sixty years of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixtieth wedding anniversary is typically marked by a couple of pensionable age.

clue.text: George has something precious to plan, I claimed

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold, a precious metal

indicators.note: claimed means the plan takes in the letter I, holding it as its own

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A man named George has a treasured scheme that the speaker says was theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is old pilots' slang for the automatic pilot, so it is no man's name here.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen jokingly nicknamed the automatic flight-control system George.

clue.text: European match won't kick off before end of work

indicators.note: a word that won't kick off loses its opening letter

parts.note: to agree is to match or correspond

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of work

explanation.surface: A football game that cannot start until a working shift finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a fixture but is the verb: AGREE loses its first letter to give GREE, then K.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Greece is a European by nationality.

clue.text: Full of stars, team like Madrid's?

parts.note: a side is a team
the Madrid football club is Real Madrid

explanation.surface: A football team packed with famous players like the Spanish giants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of stars' reads as a team of celebrities, but it means relating to the stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidereal means relating to or measured by the stars, as in sidereal time.

clue.text: Flier for the Eden project? .

parts.note: a bird suited to the garden of Eden, an earthly paradise, rather than the Cornish garden attraction

explanation.surface: A creature that might be found at the Eden Project, a botanical attraction in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eden Project is a set of giant greenhouses in Cornwall; here Eden is the biblical paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: These brightly plumed New Guinea birds are named for paradise, which Eden was.

clue.text: A northern girl has built a wonderful place

indicators.note: built means the letters are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A girl from the north has constructed an idyllic home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges A, N, GIRL and HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The hidden valley of Hilton's novel Lost Horizon became the byword for an earthly paradise.

clue.text: Very pretty daughter, though material

parts.note: twee means excessively pretty or quaint

explanation.surface: A daughter is dressed very prettily, though in something plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough woollen cloth from Scotland, it is a fabric or material.

clue.text: Eggs done soundly?

indicators.note: soundly signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: something done or finished is over

explanation.surface: Asking whether eggs have been thoroughly cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent, OVER sounds like OVA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova are egg cells, the Latin plural of ovum.

clue.text: Blooming sensational game?

definitions.note: taken as a noun, something blooming: the definition is an adjective standing for a flowering plant

parts.note: red-hot means sensational or very exciting
poker is a card game

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an exciting match, 'blooming' used as a mild oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild swear word, but it points to a flowering plant, the torch lily with spikes of red flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The kniphofia is a garden plant whose flower spikes give it this name.

clue.text: Not exactly soft or malleable

indicators.note: malleable means easily reshaped, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Something that is not quite soft, or perhaps pliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malleable' rearranges SOFT and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning approximately, roughly, in a way.

clue.text: Single soul he neglected in nick, though sweet

indicators.note: in places the single letter and the shortened soul inside the word for nick

parts.note: to nick is to steal, or take
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

indicators.note: neglected means the letters of he are left out

parts.note: the psyche is the soul or mind

explanation.surface: A lone person neglected while in prison, though sweet-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglected' removes he from the soul; 'nick' is British slang for prison, which the surface uses, but here it means steal. A tipsy cake is an old British pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: This British dessert is a trifle-like sponge soaked in wine or sherry, a pudding or sweet.

clue.text: Rejection of top novel proving problem

indicators.note: rejection sends the word back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a top or cover
Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A best-selling novel turned down, which causes a difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejection of' reverses LID to give DIL; 'novel' is not an anagram signal but Austen's book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, a predicament.

clue.text: Cocktail that's to be mixed during course of tomorrow (shortly)

indicators.note: during the course of means the mixed letters come inside the other word
shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: mañana is Spanish for tomorrow

indicators.note: to be mixed signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word that, with 's (is) as a link

explanation.surface: A cocktail that is going to be made at some point tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be mixed' rearranges the fodder and 'shortly' trims the Spanish word for tomorrow before 'during course of' puts one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a cocktail of whisky, vermouth and bitters.

clue.text: Court award given to an outdoorsy type

parts.note: to court is to woo
the DSM is the Distinguished Service Medal, a military award
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tribunal grants a prize to someone who loves the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb meaning woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives or works in the forest is an outdoor sort.

clue.text: Old play I'm to adapt for London venue

indicators.note: to adapt means to alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old drama that the speaker is going to rework for a theatre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to adapt' rearranges the play and I'm. Olympia is an exhibition hall in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is a large exhibition and events centre in Kensington, London.

clue.text: First of alternators in old banger still going

parts.note: ex- means former, old

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is an explosive, something that goes bang

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of alternators

explanation.surface: A dynamo from an old car is still working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' looks like a British slang term for an old car, but here it is the explosive TNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extant still exists, has survived and is still around.

clue.text: Lapse, opening modest drink

indicators.note: opening means the lapse splits open the modest word

parts.note: shy means modest or retiring
to err is to lapse or go wrong

explanation.surface: A slip begins a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like 'starting', but ERR opens up SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain, a drink.

clue.text: Simple catch, lead netting extraordinary red fish

parts.note: a dolly is an easy catch in cricket

indicators.note: netting means catching, so the lead takes in the rearranged red

parts.note: the van is the leading part, as in vanguard

indicators.note: extraordinary signals that the letters of red are rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler makes an easy catch, landing an unusual red fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' scrambles red before 'netting' traps it. A dolly is a cricket term for an easy catch; the fish is named after a Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dolly Varden is a North American char, a kind of trout.

clue.text: Run true, in a word?

definitions.meaning: as two words, to ... is to run away
legitimate, short for genuine or true, cut to one word

explanation.surface: Asking whether running is straight, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a word' points to the two words of the 'run' sense joined into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Legit is informal shortening of legitimate, meaning genuine; leg it is slang for flee.

clue.text: Something to contemplate held up by televangelist

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the held letters are read bottom to top
held means the letters are held within the word

explanation.surface: A religious broadcaster holds something up for meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' finds LEVAN within televangelist and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Contemplating one's belly button is the idiom for self-absorbed musing.

clue.text: Tree — after forest fire?

definitions.meaning: a common deciduous tree of the olive family
what remains when wood has burnt, the grey residue

explanation.surface: What is left of a tree after a woodland blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a timber tree and the powdery residue left by burning.

clue.text: Issue degree for hot stuff

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a mag
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: Releasing a qualification for something exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot stuff' sounds like something sexy, but it is molten rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Magma is molten rock beneath the earth's surface, very hot indeed.

clue.text: Pioneer pub tax to feed the needy, though non-starter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: to feed means the tax goes into the shortened needy word
a non-starter loses its first letter

parts.note: the needy are the poor
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A trailblazer proposing a pub levy to help the poor, though it goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-starter' looks like a verdict on the proposed tax, but it beheads the needy; 'to feed' then puts the tax inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovator introduces new ideas, a pioneer or trailblazer.

clue.text: King Cole beginning to talk with queens, becoming chatterbox

parts.note: Nat King Cole was the American singer, so Nat comes before King Cole

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of talk

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen, so two queens give two ERs

explanation.surface: The singer starts chatting with royalty and becomes a talker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Cole' is the second half of a name: Nat King Cole. ER is the crossword Queen, doubled for 'queens'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who natters talks idly and at length, a chatterbox.

clue.text: Sexy stuff of writers written in secret

indicators.note: written in means the writing fluid is put inside the secretive word

parts.note: sly means secretive or furtive
ink is what writers use

explanation.surface: Racy material that authors hide in their private notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written in' looks like part of the picture of authors, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slinky clothing clings to the body, seductively graceful and alluring.
